description: The AHEPA Hospital Model is an agent-based decision support pilot that simulates how patients reach the AHEPA tertiary hospital in Thessaloniki, Greece, when city traffic is congested or roads are disrupted. It was built at Aristotle University of Thessaloniki for the AntifragiCity project as part of Deliverable D3.4, and version 1.0 was released on Zenodo on 24 June 2026. Patients, background cars and the hospital are agents on the city's primary road network, with baseline traffic from the TomTom Traffic Index; users set city-wide traffic, patient load, congestion around the hospital and road closures, and compare three shuttle strategies, tracking throughput, efficiency, redundancy, entropy and fuel KPIs. Baseline parameters come from hospital emergency admissions between January 2023 and September 2025, which show that over 80 per cent of patients arrive by private transport. Access: NetLogo model in the repository and Zenodo archive. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a pilot for one hospital; admission records are not published. Simulation uses are hospital accessibility under disruption and emergency response planning for critical facilities. Related records: IN-CORE and other critical facility models.
